- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. # Todo

This file contains near term tasks with a short description
and reference links to more details.

Intro paragraphs in `## Todo` and `## Bugs` should begin every
line with 1 leading space so they don't match the `^\d+\. `
pattern that locates numbered entries; 2 or 3 spaces also work.

## In Progress

A cycle's record has one home at a time, and while the cycle runs this is it. At Preparation
the picked-up `## Todo` item **moves** here (never copied, one home per text) and becomes six
provisional items, all required, all revised as steps land. At close-out the whole block moves
into `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and becomes that cycle's `##` section. It is never written in
two places. Shape:

```
### <type>: <title>

#### Problem
<what is wrong, a sentence or two>

#### Solution
<what will be done about it, broad; provisional until the close-out>

#### Acceptance check
<the measure of "are you finished?">

#### Ladder
- [[N]] [<cycle title> opening][M] (done)
- [[N]] [<title>][M] (current)
- [[N]] [<title>][M]
- [[N]] <cycle title> closing

#### Deliberation
<how the five above were decided; `_None._` if there was nothing to deliberate>

#### Ladder details
<one `#####` subsection per rung, headed by its exact title, opened at laddering with the
rung's intent and completed at landing with the conceptual delta; the closing rung's only at
close-out, gotchas in problem/solution form>
```

A multi-cycle program adds one level: the program is the `###`, its current cycle the `####`,
and the six items sit one level below that (headings give the current work durable anchors,
which numbered Todo entries can't). Full rules in
[cycle-protocol.md](agent-data/cycle-protocol.md#preparation); the move's four transforms are
in [Chores sections](agent-data/cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

### docs: freshen vc-config and config subcmd

#### Problem

Both repos' `.vc-config.toml` carry a fossil `[push]` comment block from an older binary's
schema, the retired `.vc-x1` state dirs linger (empty dirs on disk, a `/.vc-x1` line in the
work `.gitignore`), generated config comments have no refresh tooling so they rot silently, and
the bot dir's `.claude` name is agent-specific where this workspace wants the neutral
`.agent-session`. Underneath those, the toml format itself caps the doc story: a `#` comment
block linkifies nothing, so a reader cannot click from a key to its documentation.

51	### docs: freshen vc-config and config subcmd
52	
53	#### Problem
54	
55	Both repos' `.vc-config.toml` carry a fossil `[push]` comment block from an older binary's
56	schema, the retired `.vc-x1` state dirs linger (empty dirs on disk, a `/.vc-x1` line in the
57	work `.gitignore`), generated config comments have no refresh tooling so they rot silently, and
58	the bot dir's `.claude` name is agent-specific where this workspace wants the neutral
59	`.agent-session`. Underneath those, the toml format itself caps the doc story: a `#` comment
60	block linkifies nothing, so a reader cannot click from a key to its documentation.
61	
62	#### Solution
63	
64	Adopt a markdown carrier for the config surface (wink, 2026-08-11), then rebuild the pipeline
65	on it. The format: a config file is a markdown document whose `toml` fences, concatenated in
66	document order, form the TOML the loader parses, so prose, per-key doc, and real reference
67	links live beside the keys they document. `vc-config-test.md` is the model rendering
68	(compact: one fence per table, doc-link bullets above it).
69	
70	- a md -> toml filter (non-fence lines blanked, so any diagnostics keep the source's line
71	  numbers) feeds the existing parser
72	  - the loader resolves `.vc-config.md`, still accepts `.vc-config.toml` for the family's
73	    migration window, and errors when a side has both
74	- the prototype `vc-config.toml` becomes `vc-config.md` in the same format: per-key `##`
75	  sections (the anchors the generated web urls land on) absorb `vc-config-design.md`, which
76	  retires, so the schema source and the browsable doc are one file
77	- the config surface adopts the agent vocabulary: `repos.agent`, `[agent-session]`, an
78	  `agent-session` subcommand and `--scope=agent`, old names accepted as aliases; the pinned
79	  prose sweep is a later convention cycle
80	- regenerate both sides' instance configs as `.vc-config.md`, retiring the fossil `[push]`
81	  comment blocks and the `.vc-x1` state-dir leftovers
82	- `config --refresh` regenerates the prose between fences while preserving fence interiors
83	  and `[repos]` byte-for-byte
84	  - a `--check` mode renders and compares without writing, exiting nonzero on any
85	    difference, so a prototype edit that skipped the refresh fails loudly
86	- add a `validate-anchors` subcommand, the validate-repo design's first standalone slice:
87	  same-file heading anchors checked via the documented slug algorithm, plus `[N]` reference
88	  resolution, across the repo's markdown records
89	- per-key worked examples in `vc-config.md`, so a reference link rewards the click
90	- repoint `repos.agent` at `.agent-session`
91	  - the directory rename itself is wink's move between sessions (a live session writes
92	    through the symlink), with the following session committing the record
93	
94	#### Acceptance check
95	
96	1. `md_to_toml` turns a config markdown file into the TOML the loader parses by
97	   concatenating its `toml` fences (line count preserved), with tests covering the model
98	   file's compact shape, the separated per-key shape, and an unclosed fence erroring.
99	2. The loader reads `.vc-config.md` on both sides, still loads a `.vc-config.toml`, and
100	   errors when a side holds both; workspace detection finds a root by either name.
101	3. build.rs generates the schema table and default constants from `vc-config.md`
102	   (rerun-if-changed wired), the hand-kept `COL_WIDTH` / `RESULT_LINE_CAP` constants are gone
103	   from `src/`, `vc-config-design.md` is gone, and each key's generated reference link lands
104	   on that key's `##` section in `vc-config.md`.
105	4. `vc-x1 config --validate` is clean on both sides, both instance files are `.vc-config.md`,
106	   and neither mentions `[push]`, `state-dir`, or `state-file`.
107	5. New surface names work with old ones as aliases: `repos.agent` / `[agent-session]` in new
108	   files while `repos.bot` / `[bot-session]` still load, and the `agent-session` subcommand
109	   answers with `bot-session` aliased to it.
110	6. `config --refresh` on a fixture with stale prose and user-edited fences preserves the
111	   fence interiors and `[repos]` while regenerating the prose (a test demonstrates it), and
112	   `--refresh --check` exits clean on both sides.
113	7. `validate-anchors` runs clean over `TODO.md`, `notes/`, `README.md`, and `vc-config.md`
114	   (same-file heading anchors and `[N]` refs), and a test shows it catching a broken anchor.
115	8. After the rename: `repos.agent = ".agent-session"`, a cycle rung pushes from a session end
116	   to end, new commits still stamp `/.claude/`-labeled ochid trailers, no `.vc-x1` dir in
117	   either repo, and no `/.vc-x1` line in `.gitignore`, which ignores the bot dir under its
118	   new name.
119	
120	#### Ladder
121	
122	- [[N]] [docs: freshen vc-config and config subcmd opening][33] (done)
123	- [[N]] [docs: separate work review stop][34] (done)
124	- [[N]] [feat: vc-config.toml prototype + build.rs codegen][35] (done)
125	- [[N]] [docs: ladder ToC + per-rung sections][36] (done)
126	- [[N]] [docs: amend cycle conventions][37] (done)
127	- [[N]] [feat: markdown config handler][38] (done)
128	- [[N]] [fix: prompt double echo][46] (done)
129	- [[N]] [feat: vc-config.md absorbs prototype and doc][39]
130	- [[N]] [feat: agent naming in config and CLI][40]
131	- [[N]] [chore: regenerate configs in md format][41]
132	- [[N]] [feat: add config --refresh][42]
133	- [[N]] [feat: add validate-anchors][43]
134	- [[N]] [docs: vc-config.md per-key examples][44]
135	- [[N]] [chore: point config at .agent-session][45]
136	- [[N]] docs: freshen vc-config and config subcmd closing
137	
138	#### Deliberation
139	
140	- the md pivot (wink, 2026-08-11): a toml instance's `#` comment blocks cannot carry a
141	  clickable link, and every patch on that (a `localfile://` scheme, taught handlers) treated
142	  the symptom
143	  - a markdown carrier dissolves it: fences hold the TOML, prose holds the doc, reference
144	    links are real markdown, and the whole spec is one sentence: the `toml` fences,
145	    concatenated in document order, must form a valid config
146	  - pivoted mid-cycle at the cheapest point: the landed prototype + codegen rungs survive
147	    unchanged, and every not-yet-landed rung was about to render the format this replaces
148	    (the `--refresh` comment-block heuristic disappears outright: prose is the generator's,
149	    fence interiors are the user's)
150	  - one format is the end state; `.toml` stays loadable through the family's migration
151	    because the internal pipeline is md -> toml, making dual support nearly free
152	  - session experiments pinned the format rules: a `[table]` header captures every key after
153	    it (TOML has no terminator), so the model is compact fences per table
154	    (vc-config-test.md), the separated per-key form falls out of the spec unadvertised, and
155	    markdown tables stay presentation-only, since parsing them re-invents what TOML does free
156	- name allocation: `vc-config.md` is the prototype-and-doc (vc-config-design.md merges in and
157	  retires), `.vc-config.md` the instance, so the derived web url's filename never changes and
158	  backlog #52 distributes the file that is both doc and schema source
159	- agent vocabulary (wink, 2026-08-11): the machine surface flips this cycle, riding the one
160	  config migration; the pinned-prose sweep ("bot repo" and kin) is its own later cycle, per
161	  "convention work runs as its own cycle"
162	- versioning (wink, 2026-08-11): no version is spoken for until it lands on main, correcting

### docs: freshen vc-config and config subcmd

#### Problem

Both repos' `.vc-config.toml` carry a fossil `[push]` comment block from an older binary's
schema, the retired `.vc-x1` state dirs linger (empty dirs on disk, a `/.vc-x1` line in the
work `.gitignore`), generated config comments have no refresh tooling so they rot silently, and
the bot dir's `.claude` name is agent-specific where this workspace wants the neutral
`.agent-session`. Underneath those, the toml format itself caps the doc story: a `#` comment
block linkifies nothing, so a reader cannot click from a key to its documentation.

#### Solution

Adopt a markdown carrier for the config surface (wink, 2026-08-11), then rebuild the pipeline
on it. The format: a config file is a markdown document whose `toml` fences, concatenated in
document order, form the TOML the loader parses, so prose, per-key doc, and real reference
links live beside the keys they document. `vc-config-test.md` is the model rendering
(compact: one fence per table, doc-link bullets above it).

- a md -> toml filter (non-fence lines blanked, so any diagnostics keep the source's line
  numbers) feeds the existing parser
  - the loader resolves `.vc-config.md`, still accepts `.vc-config.toml` for the family's
    migration window, and errors when a side has both
- the prototype `vc-config.toml` becomes `vc-config.md` in the same format: per-key `##`
  sections (the anchors the generated web urls land on) absorb `vc-config-design.md`, which
  retires, so the schema source and the browsable doc are one file
- the config surface adopts the agent vocabulary: `repos.agent`, `[agent-session]`, an
  `agent-session` subcommand and `--scope=agent`, old names accepted as aliases; the pinned
  prose sweep is a later convention cycle
- regenerate both sides' instance configs as `.vc-config.md`, retiring the fossil `[push]`
  comment blocks and the `.vc-x1` state-dir leftovers
- `config --refresh` regenerates the prose between fences while preserving fence interiors
  and `[repos]` byte-for-byte
  - a `--check` mode renders and compares without writing, exiting nonzero on any
    difference, so a prototype edit that skipped the refresh fails loudly
- add a `validate-anchors` subcommand, the validate-repo design's first standalone slice:
  same-file heading anchors checked via the documented slug algorithm, plus `[N]` reference
  resolution, across the repo's markdown records
- per-key worked examples in `vc-config.md`, so a reference link rewards the click
- repoint `repos.agent` at `.agent-session`
  - the directory rename itself is wink's move between sessions (a live session writes
    through the symlink), with the following session committing the record

#### Acceptance check

1. `md_to_toml` turns a config markdown file into the TOML the loader parses by
   concatenating its `toml` fences (line count preserved), with tests covering the model
   file's compact shape, the separated per-key shape, and an unclosed fence erroring.
2. The loader reads `.vc-config.md` on both sides, still loads a `.vc-config.toml`, and
   errors when a side holds both; workspace detection finds a root by either name.
3. build.rs generates the schema table and default constants from `vc-config.md`
   (rerun-if-changed wired), the hand-kept `COL_WIDTH` / `RESULT_LINE_CAP` constants are gone
   from `src/`, `vc-config-design.md` is gone, and each key's generated reference link lands
   on that key's `##` section in `vc-config.md`.
4. `vc-x1 config --validate` is clean on both sides, both instance files are `.vc-config.md`,
   and neither mentions `[push]`, `state-dir`, or `state-file`.
5. New surface names work with old ones as aliases: `repos.agent` / `[agent-session]` in new
   files while `repos.bot` / `[bot-session]` still load, and the `agent-session` subcommand
   answers with `bot-session` aliased to it.
6. `config --refresh` on a fixture with stale prose and user-edited fences preserves the
   fence interiors and `[repos]` while regenerating the prose (a test demonstrates it), and
   `--refresh --check` exits clean on both sides.
7. `validate-anchors` runs clean over `TODO.md`, `notes/`, `README.md`, and `vc-config.md`
   (same-file heading anchors and `[N]` refs), and a test shows it catching a broken anchor.
8. After the rename: `repos.agent = ".agent-session"`, a cycle rung pushes from a session end
   to end, new commits still stamp `/.claude/`-labeled ochid trailers, no `.vc-x1` dir in
   either repo, and no `/.vc-x1` line in `.gitignore`, which ignores the bot dir under its
   new name.

1	# custom-family.md - vc-x1's layer, as a member of the vc-x1 agent-file family
2	
3	Read after [custom.md](custom.md), whose single convention entry points here. Present only in a
4	member repo. A project that is not a member does not carry this file, and nothing in it applies
5	to one.
6	
7	**A member's `custom.md` differs from the payload by that one line, and everything of its own lives
8	here.** That is the family's convention and it buys a property worth having: `diff custom.md
9	<template>/work/custom.md` is one line for every member, so the file that can never be pinned still
10	converges, and a member's whole customization surface is this file. The medium below is here for
11	that reason rather than because it has anything to do with the family.
12	
13	## Medium and validation
14	
15	The artifact is the `vc-x1` CLI, a Rust crate (manifest `Cargo.toml`, package name `vc-x1`).
16	Versioning specifics are in [versioning.md](agent-data/versioning.md).
17	
18	**What a version bump promises**: `X.Y.Z` is a scope signal to readers of the history (see
19	[Advancing X.Y.Z](agent-data/versioning.md#advancing-xyz-scope-decides)), not a compatibility
20	contract. The crate has no library target, but the built CLI has external consumers (the family's
21	repos run it), so a change that breaks an existing invocation or the `.vc-config.toml` schema is
22	called out in the commit and surfaced by the tool's own errors rather than promised by the
23	version. Revisit with a compat clause if a library crate ever splits out.
24	
25	**Single-name convention** (adopted at the 0.78.3 cycle): the package name is the binary's
26	name, `vc-x1` on `main`, with per-line dev names on long-lived branches, guarded by `build.rs`
27	on every cargo verb. This is the project's answer to versioning.md's
28	[Dev artifact name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name): the repo is striving to
29	release, so `main` builds install as plain `vc-x1`.
30	
31	- **Full validation**
32	  - when: per-commit checklist step 5 (skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out)
33	  - run as separate invocations, each exit status checked:
34	    1. `cargo fmt`
35	    2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
36	    3. `cargo test`
37	    4. `cargo install --path . --locked`
38	    5. (re-test if anything substantive changed)
39	- **Fast validation**
40	  - when: ladder checklist step 3
41	  - `cargo test --bins`
42	
43	## Membership
44	
45	- **member name**: `vc-x1`
46	- **template repository**: `../vc-x1-template`
47	
48	These two are environment rather than instruction, the same species as `.vc-config.toml`'s
49	`[repos]` paths, and they belong there instead. They cannot move yet: `vc-x1 config --validate`
50	rejects keys it does not know, so a config carrying them would fail its own validator. The
51	`[private]` table proposal tracks the fix.
52	
53	## Messaging
54	
55	Members leave word for each other in per-member mailboxes at the template repository. The protocol
56	is `../vc-x1-template/MESSAGES.md` and it governs. These are the parts that decide how a session
57	behaves.
58	
59	- **At acquaint, check `../vc-x1-template/messages/vc-x1.md`.** An absent file means no mail.
60	- **Handle, then delete** the entry, and delete the file once it empties. Mailboxes hold open
61	  items only.
62	- **So a message can never be a record.** Anything in one worth keeping is copied into
63	  `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` *before* the entry is deleted.
64	- **Messages are thin pointers, not state.** Durable coordination state lives in topical files. A
65	  message says "action needed, see <file>" rather than restating the details.
66	- **Write to a member's mailbox, never into their repo.** A repo with a live session is written
67	  only by its own agent.
68	
69	## Dogfood log
70	
71	This project's log lives in [notes/dogfood.md](notes/dogfood.md): dated entries on where the
72	pinned instructions chafed, failed, or got amended, the evidence base for the family's
73	convergence decisions ([Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)). It stays
74	a separate file because it predates this one and is long. In-flight entries only: a resolved
75	entry retires at the beat where it resolves, per
76	[Retiring Done entries](agent-data/notes.md#retiring-done-entries).

[Advancing X.Y.Z](agent-data/versioning.md#advancing-xyz-scope-decides)), not a compatibility
contract. The crate has no library target, but the built CLI has external consumers (the family's
repos run it), so a change that breaks an existing invocation or the `.vc-config.toml` schema is
called out in the commit and surfaced by the tool's own errors rather than promised by the
version. Revisit with a compat clause if a library crate ever splits out.

**Single-name convention** (adopted at the 0.78.3 cycle): the package name is the binary's
name, `vc-x1` on `main`, with per-line dev names on long-lived branches, guarded by `build.rs`
on every cargo verb. This is the project's answer to versioning.md's
[Dev artifact name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name): the repo is striving to
release, so `main` builds install as plain `vc-x1`.

- **Full validation**
  - when: per-commit checklist step 5 (skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out)
  - run as separate invocations, each exit status checked:
    1. `cargo fmt`
    2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
    3. `cargo test`
    4. `cargo install --path . --locked`
    5. (re-test if anything substantive changed)
- **Fast validation**
  - when: ladder checklist step 3
  - `cargo test --bins`

## Membership

- **member name**: `vc-x1`
- **template repository**: `../vc-x1-template`

These two are environment rather than instruction, the same species as `.vc-config.toml`'s
`[repos]` paths, and they belong there instead. They cannot move yet: `vc-x1 config --validate`
rejects keys it does not know, so a config carrying them would fail its own validator. The
`[private]` table proposal tracks the fix.

## Messaging

Members leave word for each other in per-member mailboxes at the template repository. The protocol
is `../vc-x1-template/MESSAGES.md` and it governs. These are the parts that decide how a session
behaves.

- **At acquaint, check `../vc-x1-template/messages/vc-x1.md`.** An absent file means no mail.
- **Handle, then delete** the entry, and delete the file once it empties. Mailboxes hold open
  items only.
- **So a message can never be a record.** Anything in one worth keeping is copied into
  `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` *before* the entry is deleted.
- **Messages are thin pointers, not state.** Durable coordination state lives in topical files. A
  message says "action needed, see <file>" rather than restating the details.
- **Write to a member's mailbox, never into their repo.** A repo with a live session is written
  only by its own agent.

## Dogfood log

This project's log lives in [notes/dogfood.md](notes/dogfood.md): dated entries on where the
pinned instructions chafed, failed, or got amended, the evidence base for the family's
convergence decisions ([Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)). It stays
a separate file because it predates this one and is long. In-flight entries only: a resolved
entry retires at the beat where it resolves, per
[Retiring Done entries](agent-data/notes.md#retiring-done-entries).

1	# Cycle checklists
2	
3	Checklists for the moments where slips happen: committing, pushing, closing out. The full
4	protocol, with rationale and recovery procedures, is
5	[cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md). On any disagreement, that file wins. Re-read
6	the relevant checklist immediately before the action. Don't run it from memory.
7	
8	Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and
9	converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
10	Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).
11	
12	## The cycle at a glance
13	
14	Every change runs as a **cycle** with three phases: Preparation -> Work -> Close-out. The
15	phases always happen, but there are two styles. A **multi-step** cycle commits them
16	individually, as a ladder of steps (the Preparation commit is optional); a
17	**single-step** cycle folds all three into one commit when the change is straightforward, so
18	that one commit is the close-out and carries its duties, mandatory validation included. So a
19	single-step cycle is one commit, and a multi-step is minimum two (a Work commit plus the
20	close-out), typically three or more (the definition is
21	[AGENTS.md's Terminology](../AGENTS.md#terminology)). The
22	ladder lists a cycle's steps in order and identifies each by its title, with no number and no
23	version. Where the version-of-record lives and how often it is bumped are in
24	[versioning.md](versioning.md). Read [cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md) before any commit
25	work, and before any push, cycle or not.

protocol, with rationale and recovery procedures, is
[cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md). On any disagreement, that file wins. Re-read
the relevant checklist immediately before the action. Don't run it from memory.

Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and
converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).

## The cycle at a glance

Every change runs as a **cycle** with three phases: Preparation -> Work -> Close-out. The
phases always happen, but there are two styles. A **multi-step** cycle commits them
individually, as a ladder of steps (the Preparation commit is optional); a

single-step cycle is one commit, and a multi-step is minimum two (a Work commit plus the
close-out), typically three or more (the definition is
[AGENTS.md's Terminology](../AGENTS.md#terminology)). The
ladder lists a cycle's steps in order and identifies each by its title, with no number and no
version. Where the version-of-record lives and how often it is bumped are in

9	The `bot-session.*` keys resolve git-style, most specific wins: CLI flag, then the workspace
10	`.vc-config.toml`, then the user config (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`), then the built-in
11	default. The other keys live in a single home each: `default.*`, `repo.*`, and `account.*` in
12	the user config, `repos.*` in the workspace configs.

14	## default.account
15	
16	The account profile `init` and other account-aware commands use when `--account` is not given on
17	the command line: the name of an `[account.<name>]` section in the user config.
18	
19	## default.debug
20	
21	Reserved: the value `--debug` would assume when used without an argument. No command consumes it
22	yet; setting it is harmless and does nothing.
23	
24	## repo.default
25	
26	The repo category `--repo` assumes when given bare (no `<cat>` argument): the name of a
27	[repo.category.\<cat\>](#repocategorycat) entry, one of the built-ins (`remote`, `local`) or
28	your own.
29	
30	## repo.category.\<cat\>
31	
32	The literal value behind a repo category name: a remote url prefix (`init` appends
33	`/<NAME>.git`) or a local parent directory. `init` resolves `--repo <cat>` through this table
34	when its target is a path or a bare name.
35	
36	## account.\<name\>.repo.default
37

39	`<name>` account profile is active.
40	
41	## account.\<name\>.repo.category.\<cat\>
42	
43	Per-account variant of [repo.category.\<cat\>](#repocategorycat): a category defined inside an
44	account profile, shadowing the top-level table while that account is active.
45	
46	## bot-session.items
47	
48	The default item set the `bot-session` conversation view renders, a comma-separated list (e.g.
49	`headers,user,assistant,tool,summary`). The per-item `--<item>` / `--no-<item>` flags override
50	individual items, and `--all` / `--none` replace the base set entirely.
51	
52	## bot-session.result-lines
53	
54	Maximum lines shown per tool result in the conversation view when results are rendered; `0`
55	means unlimited. The `--result-lines` flag overrides it.
56	
57	## bot-session.col-width
58	
59	First-column width in `bot-session`'s field-inventory views: `--fields`, `--unknown`, and
60	`--per-line`. The conversation view never consults it. The built-in default aligns the type
61	column for ~99% of observed key paths: every structural key except a long tail of
62	`snapshot.trackedFileBackups.<absolute path>.*` keys, whose embedded absolute paths can be
63	arbitrarily long and so are left to overflow. The `--col-width` flag overrides it.

# vc-config: settable configuration keys

Long-form documentation for every settable vc-x1 config key, one section per key, headed by the
key's path. The `reference:` line in a generated config and in `vc-x1 config` output links to the
key's section here: build.rs derives the link from `[vc-config] reference-base` in
`vc-config.toml` (the schema prototype) plus the heading's anchor, and the test suite fails if a
key has no matching heading. Sections are in schema order.

The `bot-session.*` keys resolve git-style, most specific wins: CLI flag, then the workspace
`.vc-config.toml`, then the user config (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`), then the built-in
default. The other keys live in a single home each: `default.*`, `repo.*`, and `account.*` in
the user config, `repos.*` in the workspace configs.

## default.account

The account profile `init` and other account-aware commands use when `--account` is not given on
the command line: the name of an `[account.<name>]` section in the user config.

## default.debug

Reserved: the value `--debug` would assume when used without an argument. No command consumes it
yet; setting it is harmless and does nothing.

## repo.default

The repo category `--repo` assumes when given bare (no `<cat>` argument): the name of a
[repo.category.\<cat\>](#repocategorycat) entry, one of the built-ins (`remote`, `local`) or
your own.

## repo.category.\<cat\>

The literal value behind a repo category name: a remote url prefix (`init` appends
`/<NAME>.git`) or a local parent directory. `init` resolves `--repo <cat>` through this table
when its target is a path or a bare name.

## account.\<name\>.repo.default

Per-account variant of [repo.default](#repodefault): the default category used while the
`<name>` account profile is active.

## account.\<name\>.repo.category.\<cat\>

Per-account variant of [repo.category.\<cat\>](#repocategorycat): a category defined inside an
account profile, shadowing the top-level table while that account is active.

## bot-session.items

The default item set the `bot-session` conversation view renders, a comma-separated list (e.g.
`headers,user,assistant,tool,summary`). The per-item `--<item>` / `--no-<item>` flags override
individual items, and `--all` / `--none` replace the base set entirely.

## bot-session.result-lines

Maximum lines shown per tool result in the conversation view when results are rendered; `0`
means unlimited. The `--result-lines` flag overrides it.

## bot-session.col-width

First-column width in `bot-session`'s field-inventory views: `--fields`, `--unknown`, and
`--per-line`. The conversation view never consults it. The built-in default aligns the type
column for ~99% of observed key paths: every structural key except a long tail of
`snapshot.trackedFileBackups.<absolute path>.*` keys, whose embedded absolute paths can be
arbitrarily long and so are left to overflow. The `--col-width` flag overrides it.

## repos.work

The work repo's path, relative to the config file's directory: `"."` in the work repo, `".."`
in the bot repo. Structural: written by `init`, read by workspace-root discovery, and the entry
that resolves to the config's own directory names that file's side. Every `.vc-config.toml`
must carry it.

## repos.bot

The bot repo's path, relative to the config file's directory (e.g. `".claude"` in the work
repo, `"."` in the bot repo). Its presence is what signals dual-repo mode; a single-repo
workspace simply omits it.

input.description: Read README sections on config schema

content.content:
|------|-------------|
| `-R, --repo <PATH>` | Path to the bot repo [default: .claude] |

`vc-x1 squash-push` reports the condition and proceeds, since publishing is its job. `vc-x1 push` no
longer checks it: a bot repo that hasn't been squash-pushed yet isn't a broken state, and the next
push publishes it anyway.

### config

Print the settable config keys for a target config file as an annotated, commented schema: for each
key its description, the command/context it's `used by`, its default (or a value marked `# example`
when there is no default), a `reference` url pointing at that key's documentation, and a commented
assignment line ready to paste in. The schema is generated at build time from the `vc-config.toml`
prototype at the repo root (see
[vc-config.toml (the schema prototype)](#vc-configtoml-the-schema-prototype)), so it can't drift
from what the code actually reads.

- `[TARGET]`: `work`, `bot`, `work,bot` (default), or an explicit config-file path. The keywords
  resolve against the surrounding workspace's `.vc-config.toml` files and filter to that side's
  keys; a path carries no side information, so it gets the whole schema. The user config
  (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`) has no keyword and is reached only by passing its path.
- `--validate`: instead of printing, load the target's actual config file(s) and flag any key the
  schema doesn't recognize (a typo, a key in the wrong section, or an unknown key), plus, for
  keyword targets, the legacy-schema rejection and the resolved-agreement invariant of a dual
  workspace's `[repos]` registries. Exits non-zero if any problem is found. This is an opt-in strict
  check; a normal config load silently ignores unknown keys, for forward-compatibility.

A short sample of the printed schema (workspace home):

```
[bot-session]
# bot-session.col-width: Default --col-width: first-column width in the
#   --fields / --unknown / --per-line views
#   used by: bot-session --col-width
#   default: 68
#   reference: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/HEAD/vc-config.md#bot-sessioncol-width
# col-width = 68

[repos]
# repos.work: The work repo's path, relative to this config file's
#   directory ("." in the work repo, ".." in the bot repo); the entry
# Check one explicit file
vc-x1 config ../other/.vc-config.toml --validate

# vc-config: settable configuration keys

This file is two things at once, and that is the point: the **schema prototype** vc-x1 is built
from, and the **long-form documentation** every generated `reference:` url lands on. One `##`
section per settable key holds that key's prose and, in a `toml` fence, that key's metadata, so
the documentation and the schema cannot describe different keys.

It is not a config file. Your workspace's config is `.vc-config.md` (note the leading dot).
Editing this file changes what the binary knows, takes effect on the next build, and is reviewed
like any source change.

## How this file is read

The format is the config markdown carrier's own: the `toml` fences, concatenated in document
order, form the TOML that gets parsed. build.rs shares the filter (`src/md_fence.rs`) with the
instance-config loader, so the prototype and a `.vc-config.md` are read by one rule, and prose
outside the fences never reaches a parser.

Shape: one TOML table per settable key, named by the key's path, dynamic segments quoted
(`[repo.category."<cat>"]`). Key order here is rendering order everywhere downstream. The
entries a key's table may carry:

- `homes`: which config file(s) accept the key: `"user"` (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`),
  `"workspace-code"`, `"workspace-bot"` (the two instance-config sides)
- `kind`: value shape, one of `"str"`, `"usize"`, `"item-list"`
- `doc`: one-line description (rendered into generated configs, so keep it tight)
- `used-by`: the command/flag or structural context consuming it
- `default`: the built-in value; omit when there is none
- `example`: representative value for keys with no default
- `required`: active (not commented) in generated configs; the value is role-specific, filled by
  `init`
- `reference`: optional override url for the key's docs; when absent (the norm) build.rs derives
  `<reference-base>/blob/HEAD/vc-config.md#<anchor of the path>`, which is the key's own section
  below

## The prototype's own metadata

`[vc-config]` is this file's metadata rather than a settable key. `reference-base` is the bare
repo url every derived reference is built from: build.rs joins it with `/blob/HEAD/vc-config.md#`
and the key's heading anchor, so a reference follows the repo's default branch and no branch name
is baked in. A fork points it at its own repo and edits its own copy of this file.

```toml
[vc-config]
reference-base = "https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1"
```

## How the keys resolve

The `bot-session.*` keys resolve git-style, most specific wins: CLI flag, then the workspace
instance config, then the user config (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`), then the built-in default.
The other keys live in a single home each: `default.*`, `repo.*`, and `account.*` in the user
config, `repos.*` in the workspace configs.

## default.account

The account profile `init` and other account-aware commands use when `--account` is not given on
the command line: the name of an `[account.<name>]` section in the user config.

```toml
[default.account]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Account profile (an [account.<name>] section) to use when --account is absent"
used-by = "--account (init and account-aware commands)"
example = "work"
```

## default.debug

Reserved: the value `--debug` would assume when used without an argument. No command consumes it
yet; setting it is harmless and does nothing.

```toml
[default.debug]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Default --debug value when used without an argument (reserved; not yet consumed)"
used-by = "--debug (reserved; not yet consumed)"
example = "true"
```

## repo.default

The repo category `--repo` assumes when given bare (no `<cat>` argument): the name of a
[repo.category.\<cat\>](#repocategorycat) entry, one of the built-ins (`remote`, `local`) or
your own.

```toml
[repo.default]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Default repo category when --repo is bare: a [repo.category.<cat>] name: a built-in (remote, local) or your own"
used-by = "--repo (default category when --repo is bare)"
example = "acmehousing"
```

## repo.category.\<cat\>

The literal value behind a repo category name: a remote url prefix (`init` appends
`/<NAME>.git`) or a local parent directory. `init` resolves `--repo <cat>` through this table
when its target is a path or a bare name.

```toml
[repo.category."<cat>"]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Literal value for repo category <cat>: a remote URL prefix (init appends /<NAME>.git) or a local parent dir"
used-by = "--repo <cat> (init remote/local resolution)"
example = "git@github.com:acmehousing"
```

## account.\<name\>.repo.default

Per-account variant of [repo.default](#repodefault): the default category used while the
`<name>` account profile is active.

```toml
[account."<name>".repo.default]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Per-account default repo category: a [repo.category.<cat>] name: a built-in (remote, local) or your own"
used-by = "--account <name> with --repo"
example = "acmehousing"
```

## account.\<name\>.repo.category.\<cat\>

Per-account variant of [repo.category.\<cat\>](#repocategorycat): a category defined inside an
account profile, shadowing the top-level table while that account is active.

```toml
[account."<name>".repo.category."<cat>"]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Per-account literal value for repo category <cat> (remote URL prefix or local parent dir)"
used-by = "--account <name> with --repo <cat>"
example = "git@github.com:acmehousing"
```

## bot-session.items

The default item set the `bot-session` conversation view renders, a comma-separated list (e.g.
`headers,user,assistant,tool,summary`). The per-item `--<item>` / `--no-<item>` flags override
individual items, and `--all` / `--none` replace the base set entirely.

```toml
[bot-session.items]
homes = ["user", "workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]
kind = "item-list"
doc = "Default bot-session item set (comma-separated)"
used-by = "bot-session --<item> / --no-<item> / --all / --none"
default = "headers,user,assistant,tool,summary"
```

## bot-session.result-lines

Maximum lines shown per tool result in the conversation view when results are rendered; `0`
means unlimited. The `--result-lines` flag overrides it.

```toml
[bot-session.result-lines]
homes = ["user", "workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]
kind = "usize"
doc = "Default --result-lines: max lines shown per tool result (0 = unlimited)"
used-by = "bot-session --result-lines"
default = 10
```

## bot-session.col-width

First-column width in `bot-session`'s field-inventory views: `--fields`, `--unknown`, and
`--per-line`. The conversation view never consults it. The built-in default aligns the type
column for ~99% of observed key paths: every structural key except a long tail of
`snapshot.trackedFileBackups.<absolute path>.*` keys, whose embedded absolute paths can be
arbitrarily long and so are left to overflow. The `--col-width` flag overrides it.

```toml
[bot-session.col-width]
homes = ["user", "workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]
kind = "usize"
doc = "Default --col-width: first-column width in the --fields / --unknown / --per-line views"
used-by = "bot-session --col-width"
default = 68
```

## repos.work

The work repo's path, relative to the config file's directory: `"."` in the work repo, `".."`
in the bot repo. Structural: written by `init`, read by workspace-root discovery, and the entry
that resolves to the config's own directory names that file's side. Every instance config must
carry it.

```toml
[repos.work]
homes = ["workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]
kind = "str"
doc = "The work repo's path, relative to this config file's directory (\".\" in the work repo, \"..\" in the bot repo); the entry resolving to the config's own directory names the side"
used-by = "find_workspace_root, side detection (structural; written by init)"
required = true
example = "."
```

## repos.bot

The bot repo's path, relative to the config file's directory (e.g. `".claude"` in the work
repo, `"."` in the bot repo). Its presence is what signals dual-repo mode; a single-repo
workspace simply omits it.

```toml
[repos.bot]
homes = ["workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]
kind = "str"
doc = "The bot repo's path, relative to this config file's directory (e.g. \".claude\" in the work repo, \".\" in the bot repo); presence signals dual-repo mode"
used-by = "default_scope, scope resolution, ochid prefixes (structural)"
example = ".claude"
```

The literal value behind a repo category name: a remote url prefix (`init` appends
`/<NAME>.git`) or a local parent directory. `init` resolves `--repo <cat>` through this table
when its target is a path or a bare name.

```toml
[repo.category."<cat>"]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Literal value for repo category <cat>: a remote URL prefix (init appends /<NAME>.git) or a local parent dir"
used-by = "--repo <cat> (init remote/local resolution)"
example = "git@github.com:acmehousing"
```

## account.\<name\>.repo.default

Per-account variant of [repo.default](#repodefault): the default category used while the
`<name>` account profile is active.

```toml
[account."<name>".repo.default]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Per-account default repo category: a [repo.category.<cat>] name: a built-in (remote, local) or your own"
used-by = "--account <name> with --repo"
example = "acmehousing"
```

## account.\<name\>.repo.category.\<cat\>

Per-account variant of [repo.category.\<cat\>](#repocategorycat): a category defined inside an
account profile, shadowing the top-level table while that account is active.

```toml
[account."<name>".repo.category."<cat>"]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Per-account literal value for repo category <cat> (remote URL prefix or local parent dir)"
used-by = "--account <name> with --repo <cat>"
example = "git@github.com:acmehousing"
```

## bot-session.items

The default item set the `bot-session` conversation view renders, a comma-separated list (e.g.
`headers,user,assistant,tool,summary`). The per-item `--<item>` / `--no-<item>` flags override
individual items, and `--all` / `--none` replace the base set entirely.

```toml
[bot-session.items]
homes = ["user", "workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]
kind = "item-list"
doc = "Default bot-session item set (comma-separated)"
used-by = "bot-session --<item> / --no-<item> / --all / --none"
default = "headers,user,assistant,tool,summary"
```

## bot-session.result-lines

Maximum lines shown per tool result in the conversation view when results are rendered; `0`
means unlimited. The `--result-lines` flag overrides it.

```toml
[bot-session.result-lines]
homes = ["user", "workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]
kind = "usize"
doc = "Default --result-lines: max lines shown per tool result (0 = unlimited)"
used-by = "bot-session --result-lines"
default = 10
```

## bot-session.col-width

First-column width in `bot-session`'s field-inventory views: `--fields`, `--unknown`, and
`--per-line`. The conversation view never consults it. The built-in default aligns the type
column for ~99% of observed key paths: every structural key except a long tail of
`snapshot.trackedFileBackups.<absolute path>.*` keys, whose embedded absolute paths can be
arbitrarily long and so are left to overflow. The `--col-width` flag overrides it.

```toml
[bot-session.col-width]
homes = ["user", "workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]
kind = "usize"
doc = "Default --col-width: first-column width in the --fields / --unknown / --per-line views"
used-by = "bot-session --col-width"
default = 68
```

## repos.work

The work repo's path, relative to the config file's directory: `"."` in the work repo, `".."`
in the bot repo. Structural: written by `init`, read by workspace-root discovery, and the entry
that resolves to the config's own directory names that file's side. Every instance config must
carry it.

```toml
[repos.work]
homes = ["workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]
kind = "str"
doc = "The work repo's path, relative to this config file's directory (\".\" in the work repo, \"..\" in the bot repo); the entry resolving to the config's own directory names the side"
used-by = "find_workspace_root, side detection (structural; written by init)"
required = true
example = "."
```

## repos.bot

The bot repo's path, relative to the config file's directory (e.g. `".claude"` in the work
repo, `"."` in the bot repo). Its presence is what signals dual-repo mode; a single-repo
workspace simply omits it.

```toml
[repos.bot]
homes = ["workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]
kind = "str"
doc = "The bot repo's path, relative to this config file's directory (e.g. \".claude\" in the work repo, \".\" in the bot repo); presence signals dual-repo mode"
used-by = "default_scope, scope resolution, ochid prefixes (structural)"
example = ".claude"
```

### vc-config.toml (the schema prototype)

`vc-config.toml` at the repo root (no leading dot) is the single source of truth for the
settable-key schema above. It is not a config file: each settable key is a TOML table of that
key's metadata, and build.rs parses the file and generates the schema table plus the built-in
default constants the binary compiles against. One file drives every surface:

default = 68

# Architecture

How the `vc-x1` binary is structured: the clap-aware CLI layer
and the (emerging) clap-free subcommand layer. This is the
"what + some why" — generic and slow-moving. The *how* and the
per-cycle / per-subcommand status live in `notes/chores/chores-*.md`
and `TODO.md`.

This is a living document; the tool is under continuous
development and the repo will keep changing.

## Overview

`vc-x1` is a single binary that supports subcommands,
`vc-x1 <subcommand>`, for managing a jj-git **dual-repo workspace**
with a work repo plus a `.claude` bot repo. The commits
cross-reference each other via `ochid:` trailers at the bottom
of each commit message. See [`README.md`](README.md) for the
user-facing picture and [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) for the bot
workflow.

## Two layers: CLI args vs subcommand Context + Params

Goal: separate clap-aware argument parsing from subcommand
operation logic, so a future front-end (TUI, library embedding)
can call the same core without dragging clap along. The trigger
was `args.account.account`-style nested-leaf access leaking into
subcommand bodies; accessor shortcuts were rejected as hiding
the mismatch rather than fixing it.

- **CLI layer (clap-aware)**: builds `XxxParams` from the
  user-facing `XxxArgs` `#[derive(Args)]` clap struct.
  Options/flags used in more than one subcommand live as
  flattened leaves/bundles in `src/options_flags/`.
- **Subcommand layer (clap-free)**: entrypoint shape
  `fn x(ctx: &Context, params: &XxxParams) -> Result<…>` —
  isolates the subcommand from clap and from the user.
  - `Context` — platform state shared by every subcommand.
  - `XxxParams` — that subcommand's inputs, derived from
    config / command-line args.
- **Boundary conversion**: `XxxArgs → XxxParams` via
  `impl From<&XxxArgs>` or `impl TryFrom<&XxxArgs>`, depending
  on whether the conversion can fail.

Two parameters per subcommand; the signature documents what the
subcommand depends on. `Context` is the same across all
subcommands; `XxxParams` carry the per-subcommand inputs.

Rules for the subcommand layer (some still aspirational — see
[the Context+Params port](#args--context--params)):

1. Plain options, flat fields, `Default` — no clap types in
   `XxxParams`. Domain types (`RepoSelector`, `Scope`) are
   fine; leaf wrappers (`RepoOption`) are not.
2. Typed errors (`enum XError`, not `Box<dyn Error>`) — a TUI
   matches variants to pick dialogs; CLI formats them.
3. Returned outcomes, not `println!` — each subcommand returns
   a structured result; CLI formats it, a library writes
   nothing to stdout itself.
4. Progress via an optional `&mut dyn ProgressSink` on
   long-running subcommands — CLI installs a stderr sink, tests
   a recording sink.
5. No globals, no implicit cwd/env reads in subcommands — CLI
   resolves cwd/env once at startup and builds `Context`.

None of this is sacred — the whole structure is an experiment.
The current scope is deliberately narrow: a small `Context`
(two params, not one god blob); no trait-based DI yet; one
crate, not a workspace split; `src/options_flags/` leaves left
in place — only their consumers change shape. Widen any of it
when the evidence (a second front-end, a second consumer crate,
a real platform-surface divergence) calls for it — not before.

### Naming

Earlier drafts of this design used `Workspace` / `XOptions`;
the implementation (0.44.0) chose `Context` / `XxxParams`:

- `Workspace` → `Context` — Cargo owns "workspace" formally,
  and this codebase already uses "workspace" for the dual-repo
  project root (`find_workspace_root`).
- `XOptions` → `XxxParams` — avoids visual collision with
  `Option<T>` (a params struct mixes required and
  `Option<T>`-typed fields) and with `src/options_flags/`.

## Module map

The *kinds* of module and what they're for — not an exhaustive
catalog (read the `//!` docstrings; `notes/chores/chores-*.md` for
per-subcommand refactor status):

**CLI layer:**

- `src/main.rs` — the clap edge: `Cli` (`Parser`), `Commands`
  (`Subcommand`) + the dispatch arms, `cli_with_banner()` (the
  per-subcommand `vc-x1 X.Y.Z` banner), `CompleteEnv` wiring,
  and `bm_track` (the permanent `main`-bookmark tracking
  diagnostic on every command's entry/exit).
- `src/options_flags/` — reusable `#[derive(Args)]` *leaves*
  (one flag, or a small fixed pair) and *bundles*
  (`#[command(flatten)]` of N leaves) shared across
  subcommands, so a flag is defined (parser, help, completer)
  exactly once. See
  [`src/options_flags/README.md`](src/options_flags/README.md).
- `src/common.rs` — helpers the read-only commit-query
  subcommands (`chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show`) share:
  `for_each_repo`, `collect_ids`, `resolve_revset`, the
  `DotSpec` / `..`-notation parsing, `Header` /
  `resolve_header`, the `format_*` printers, and the
  `-R`/`-s` resolution stack — `find_workspace_root` /
  `default_scope` / `scope_to_repos` / `resolve_repos`
  (the top-level entry combining the `-R PATH` override and
  the `-s code|bot|code,bot` role selection).
- `src/jj.rs` — the typed facade over `jj` subprocess
  queries (`log` templates and bookmark listings):
  `matches` / `rev_exists`, `chid_of` / `cid_of` /
  `cid_short_of`, `desc_of` / `is_empty`,
  `bookmark_list[_all]`. Mutations still spawn `jj` at
  their call sites until the refactor program's jj-lib
  migration stage moves both in-process
  ([refactor-20260716.md](notes/refactor-20260716.md)).

**Subcommand-layer scaffolding:**

- `src/context.rs` — `Context`, the shared platform handle
  (today: the loaded `UserConfig` + the `--log` path; built
  once at startup via `Context::load(log)`).
- `src/config.rs` — `UserConfig` (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`).
- `src/options_flags/scope.rs` — `Scope` (a newtype over
  `Vec<Side>` — the `code`/`bot` role set) and `parse_scope`.

**Subcommand modules** — `src/<x>.rs` holds the subcommand's
`XxxArgs` (`#[derive(Args)]`, composing `options_flags/` leaves
where one exists) and the entrypoint `pub fn x(...)`. Modules:
`chid`, `desc` (+ `desc_helpers`), `list`, `show`,
`validate_desc`, `fix_desc`, `validate_todo` / `fix_todo`
(+ `todo_helpers`), `validate_bot`, `clone`, `init`
(+ `init/params`), `symlink`, `sync`,
`squash_push`, `push`,
`config_cmd`, `bot_session` (+ `transcript`). Which ones have ported to `(ctx, params)` and which
compose `options_flags/` leaves: `notes/chores/chores-*.md` +
`TODO.md`.

**Support:**

- `src/repo_utils.rs`, `src/url.rs`, `src/toml_simple.rs`,
  `src/logging.rs` — jj/repo helpers, URL parsing, a minimal
  TOML reader, the CLI logger.
- `src/test_helpers.rs`, `src/test_tmp_root.rs` —
  `#[cfg(test)]` fixtures and tempdir resolution. Subcommand
  modules also carry their own `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (and
  `integration_tests` for `sync` / `push`).

## Subcommand model

Adding a subcommand `x`:

1. Create `src/x.rs` with `pub struct XxxArgs`
   (`#[derive(Args)]`), composing leaves from
   `src/options_flags/` where one exists.
2. Add a variant `X(x::XxxArgs)` to `Commands` in `src/main.rs`
   with a `///` summary (and `#[command(long_about = …)]` for
   the long form).
3. Add a dispatch arm in `main()` calling `x::x(&args)` (or,
   once ported, `x::x(&ctx, &params)`).
4. Doc comments on `#[arg(...)]` fields drive `--help`; add
   `#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, …)]` on any field whose doc
   comment uses bullets (clap otherwise reflows them into
   prose).
5. Dynamic value completion (`--account=<TAB>`) is an
   `ArgValueCompleter` attached to the leaf in
   `src/options_flags/` — completion is a clap-aware concern
   and stays at this layer.

## args → Context + Params

"The Context+Params port" — each subcommand's
`pub fn x(args: &XxxArgs)` is structured as
`pub fn x(ctx: &Context, params: &XxxParams)`, with an
`XxxParams` flat struct + a `From` (or `TryFrom`, if the

0.49.0, and the shape new subcommands follow. Out of scope

status: `notes/chores/chores-*.md` (the "Refactor tracking" section).

Independently of the Context+Params port — "the options_flags
extraction" — per-subcommand inline `#[arg]` fields are being
lifted into reusable leaves/bundles under `src/options_flags/`
so a flag is defined (parser, help, completer) exactly once. See
[`src/options_flags/README.md`](src/options_flags/README.md)
for the leaf / bundle / Pattern-A mechanics and the
Flag-vs-Option classification; `notes/chores/chores-*.md` for
per-subcommand status.

153:## Suffix scheme
154-
155-The cycle (Preparation -> Work -> Close-out, per [cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md)) encodes
156-each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a Preparation**.
157-
158-This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is
159-not a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries
160-neither a number nor a version (see
161-[Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)). The one
162-prose surface that records a version is a chores as-built rung, where it is a property of a landed
163-commit sitting beside that commit's SHA. The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and
164-nothing dereferences one.
165-
166-- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
167-- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: Work commits
168-- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)
169-
170-**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0`
171-and starts at `-1` (its first Work commit). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle needing no
172-Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0` step
173-without renumbering siblings.

Reviewed. Your rewrite fixes the real problem (the old intro never said what a reader is looking at), so I kept its shape and fixed what's wrong underneath.

## Findings in the draft

**Factual**

1. `.vc-config.md:4` — "The other repo ... **is** also a markdown configuration file". A repo isn't a file; it *has* one. This is the sentence a neophyte would misread hardest.
2. `.vc-config.md:9` — "during **complication**" should be "compilation".
3. `.vc-config.md:4` — "**typically** named `.vc-config.md`". It isn't typical, it's the name the loader resolves. (`.vc-config.toml` is accepted for the family's migration window, which a neophyte doesn't need.)
4. `.vc-config.md:12` — "is **an** simple version".

**Convention**

5. "work-repo" / "agent-repo": AGENTS.md Terminology says two words, hyphen only directly in front of another noun. So "work repo", but "work-repo commit".
6. "agent repo" in prose sits one rung ahead of the fence, which still says `bot = ".claude"`. The next rung (`feat: agent naming in config and CLI`) flips the key. I'd let the word and the key flip together there rather than leave them disagreeing for a rung.

**Structural, and the one that matters most**

7. **This prose is machine-owned.** The ownership model settled at the regenerate rung: fence interiors are the workspace's, the prose between them is the generator's rendering. So whatever we agree here isn't a one-file edit, it's the **generator's template**, and it has to be written to parameterize: the side (work vs agent) and dual-repo vs POR, since paragraph 3 has nothing to say in a single-repo workspace.

## Proposed intro

Work side. The agent side differs only in "this copy is the *agent* repo's" and the path in paragraph 3, and paragraph 3 is omitted entirely for POR:

```markdown
# vc-x1 config file

This file configures vc-x1 for one repo, and this copy is the work repo's.

Only the `toml` code blocks below are configuration. vc-x1 concatenates them in the order they
appear and reads the result as a single TOML document. Every other line, this sentence included,
is documentation that no parser ever sees, which is the point of the format: a setting can be
explained right where it is set.

This workspace is a pair of repos, and each one configures itself. The other is at `.claude`,
and its own `.vc-config.md` names these same two paths from its side.

[vc-config.md](vc-config.md) documents the settable keys, one section per key, and the numbered
links above each block point at that key's section. vc-x1 is built from that same file, so it is
also the list of keys a config may use: `vc-x1 config --validate` reports any key that is not on
it.

[vc-config-model.md](vc-config-model.md) is a fuller example, every table and key present at a
typical value, to copy from.
```

The model file takes paragraphs 2 and 4 verbatim, and swaps 1/3/5 for one opener:

```markdown
# vc-x1 config file: the model

This file is a model, not a live config: it shows the format with every table and key present at
a typical value. Copy from it. Nothing reads it.
```

## On the rename

**`vc-config-model.md`, yes.** "Model" is already the word in this cycle's records and in `config_md.rs`'s fixture doc comment ("The model rendering"), so the rename makes the file agree with the vocabulary rather than introducing a third one. Nothing reads the file programmatically today, so the rename is prose-only.

One caution on "every table and key/value pair showing typical or default values": a hand-kept every-key file is precisely the drift this cycle exists to kill, and it would rot the same way the fossil `[push]` block did. Two ways out, and I'd take the second:

- generate it, like the instance configs, at `config --refresh` time
- keep it hand-written but **test-pinned**: a test parses it and asserts its key set equals the schema's, so adding a key to `vc-config.md` without updating the model fails the suite

The second keeps the file readable as a teaching artifact (a generated one reads like generated output) while making silence impossible.

**The plain version:** your rewrite is the right idea; it has four small errors, uses hyphenated repo names the conventions don't, and says "agent" one rung before the config key does. The bigger point is that this paragraph is going to be printed by the generator, not typed, so we should agree it as a template with the side and the dual/POR bits parameterized. `vc-config-model.md` is a good name, and if it's going to list every key it needs a test tying it to the schema.

Want me to apply this as a rider on the current rung, or hold it for the regenerate rung where the generator gets written?

content.text:
Agreeing, with three corrections and one push-back.

## Where you're right, and more right than I was

I argued the live config and the model are different artifacts. Checking `init.rs`, they never were: `render_settable_keys_block` already writes **every settable key, commented, at its default** into a generated config. The full-key file *is* the generated instance. My "a ~150-line file where 4 lines matter" objection was about the interim hand-written stub we're running on now, not about the real output. Byte-identity isn't a new constraint, it's naming one the generator already satisfies.

And commented keys inside a `toml` fence are TOML comments, so a full-key model sets nothing. Behaviorally identical to the 19-line stub, which is what makes byte-identity safe at all.

## Three corrections

1. **Drop the "fuller example" paragraph.** Byte-identical means the model would point at itself. It isn't needed once the live config *is* the full example.
2. **It models the work side only.** The agent side can't be byte-identical to it: `[repos]` values invert, the doc links need `../`, and the side sentence differs. Three differences, all forced. The model demonstrates the format; the agent side is the format applied to the other role.
3. **Byte-identity has to be enforced, not asserted.** A test rendering the work role and comparing to the checked-in `vc-config-model.md`. Without it we've written down an intention, which is the failure mode this whole cycle exists to fix.

## The push-back

Not on the idea. On calling it a rider on the current rung.

Deciding what a generated md instance *looks like* — where the doc links sit, one fence per table or per key, what survives of the `#`-comment blocks — is the `chore: regenerate configs in md format` rung's central design question. Writing the model now doesn't avoid that work, it **is** that work, done spec-first. That's the better order, and it's worth its own commit for two reasons: this rung's title doesn't promise a model file, and the regenerate rung then has something to be diffed against instead of eyeballed.

So: insert a rung after this one.

- **`docs: vc-config-model.md, the generated config's target`** — the rename, the full-key hand-written model, `.vc-config.md` byte-identical to it, the agent side rewritten to match modulo its role.
- The regenerate rung's job collapses to "make the generator emit exactly this", and its acceptance becomes mechanical: `--refresh --check` exits clean and changes no byte.

The current rung is validated and complete; it hasn't pushed, so adding the new rung to the ladder is a free edit that rides in its records.

One practical note for that rung: the per-key prose is already written (it's `vc-config.md`'s section text, one-liners in the `doc` fields), so the model is mostly assembly plus the format judgment. Not a large rung, but a decision-dense one.

One thing to flag rather than fix: the model's `[repos]` will carry this workspace's real values (`work = "."`, `bot = ".claude"`). Correct for a model of this workspace, and a reader could copy `.claude` without thinking. I'd leave it and let the prose carry the caveat.

**The plain version:** yes to byte-identical, and your reasoning beat mine — the generator already writes full-key configs, so this is naming an existing property rather than adding a constraint. Drop the self-referential paragraph, accept that only the work side can match, and add a test that renders and compares. But make it its own rung rather than a rider, because writing the model *is* the regenerate rung's design work, just done first, and it should be a commit the generator can be diffed against.

Shall I ladder it in as the next rung?

Your reorder is right, and the reason you gave is load-bearing in a way the layout doesn't show. Chasing it turned up two defects.

## Finding A: `bot-session` can't read this workspace's config at all

`src/bot_session.rs:792` reads `root.join(".vc-config.toml")` through `toml_simple::toml_load`, bypassing `config_md::load`. Both sides of this workspace now hold only `.vc-config.md`, so `path.exists()` is false and the function returns all-`None` and falls through to the user config and built-in defaults. Silently — no error, no warning.

This is a live regression from the handler rung's carrier switch. That rung's records claim `config_md::load` is the one loader every reader goes through; the claim was scoped to *topology* readers, and this scalar reader was never converted. It's also the exact silent-degrade the same rung fixed elsewhere ("a present-but-unloadable config now marks the workspace root instead of being walked past").

Read from the code, not demonstrated: the branch is unconditional on `exists()` and there is no `.vc-config.toml` at either root.

## Finding B: the schema says the bot side accepts `[bot-session]`. Nothing reads it there.

You said `bot-session` is work-side only. The code agrees: `workspace_bot_session()` consults `find_workspace_root()`, which is the work root, and never the bot side's file. But `vc-config.md` declares `homes = ["user", "workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]` for all three keys, so today:

- `vc-x1 config bot` advertises them as settable on the bot side
- `init` writes commented `[bot-session]` blocks into the bot-side config
- `config --validate` accepts them there

and none of it is ever read. Your new sentence — "Its own `.vc-config.md` carries only the `[repos]` table" — is what we *want* to be true and is false today.

I'd fix it toward the code: `homes = ["user", "workspace-code"]`. The alternative, teaching the reader to consult both sides, needs a precedence rule between two workspace files that doesn't exist. `[repos]` gets away with living on both sides only because it has the resolved-agreement invariant forcing them to match; a behavioral key has no such thing.

## Two edits applied to the draft

- The `.claude` sentence had a splice from the reorder ("and its own `.vc-config.md`. It only uses the [repos] table names these same two paths"). Rewritten to say the bot side carries `[repos]` only.
- "at its built-in default, uncomment it" was a comma splice. Two sentences — prose.md's Semicolons section rules out the semicolon too, since this is instruction-after-claim rather than two parallel claims.

## Where I'd put the two findings

- **B** into the model rung. Deciding the bot side's shape *is* that rung, and the `homes` line is what makes your sentence true.
- **A** as its own small rung ahead of it, `fix: bot-session reads the md carrier`. It's a code bug this cycle introduced, unrelated to the model, and it should not ride inside a docs commit.

Neither belongs in the current rung — its title promises the absorb and nothing else.

**The plain version:** moving `[repos]` first was right, and the reason you gave for it exposed a schema lie: the bot side is advertised as accepting `bot-session` keys that nothing reads. Separately, `bot-session` currently can't read *either* side's config, because it still looks for the `.toml` file we stopped writing. I fixed the two prose slips in the draft. I'd like your go to ladder those two fixes in as rungs, and I have not touched anything outside `tmp/` for them.

# vc-config: settable configuration keys

This file is two things at once, and that is the point: the **schema prototype** vc-x1 is built
from, and the **long-form documentation** every generated `reference:` url lands on. One `##`
section per settable key holds that key's prose and, in a `toml` fence, that key's metadata, so
the documentation and the schema cannot describe different keys.

It is not a config file. Your workspace's config is `.vc-config.md` (note the leading dot).
Editing this file changes what the binary knows, takes effect on the next build, and is reviewed
like any source change.

## How this file is read

The format is the config markdown carrier's own: the `toml` fences, concatenated in document
order, form the TOML that gets parsed. build.rs shares the filter (`src/md_fence.rs`) with the
instance-config loader, so the prototype and a `.vc-config.md` are read by one rule, and prose
outside the fences never reaches a parser.

Shape: one TOML table per settable key, named by the key's path, dynamic segments quoted
(`[repo.category."<cat>"]`). Key order here is rendering order everywhere downstream. The
entries a key's table may carry:

- `homes`: which config file(s) accept the key: `"user"` (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`),
  `"workspace-code"`, `"workspace-bot"` (the two instance-config sides)
- `kind`: value shape, one of `"str"`, `"usize"`, `"item-list"`
- `doc`: one-line description (rendered into generated configs, so keep it tight)
- `used-by`: the command/flag or structural context consuming it
- `default`: the built-in value; omit when there is none
- `example`: representative value for keys with no default
- `required`: active (not commented) in generated configs; the value is role-specific, filled by
  `init`
- `reference`: optional override url for the key's docs; when absent (the norm) build.rs derives
  `<reference-base>/blob/HEAD/vc-config.md#<anchor of the path>`, which is the key's own section
  below

## The prototype's own metadata

`[vc-config]` is this file's metadata rather than a settable key. `reference-base` is the bare
repo url every derived reference is built from: build.rs joins it with `/blob/HEAD/vc-config.md#`
and the key's heading anchor, so a reference follows the repo's default branch and no branch name
is baked in. A fork points it at its own repo and edits its own copy of this file.

```toml
[vc-config]
reference-base = "https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1"
```

## How the keys resolve

The `bot-session.*` keys resolve git-style, most specific wins: CLI flag, then the workspace
instance config, then the user config (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`), then the built-in default.
The other keys live in a single home each: `default.*`, `repo.*`, and `account.*` in the user
config, `repos.*` in the workspace configs.

## default.account

The account profile `init` and other account-aware commands use when `--account` is not given on
the command line: the name of an `[account.<name>]` section in the user config.

```toml
[default.account]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Account profile (an [account.<name>] section) to use when --account is absent"
used-by = "--account (init and account-aware commands)"
example = "work"
```

## default.debug

Reserved: the value `--debug` would assume when used without an argument. No command consumes it
yet; setting it is harmless and does nothing.

```toml
[default.debug]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Default --debug value when used without an argument (reserved; not yet consumed)"
used-by = "--debug (reserved; not yet consumed)"
example = "true"
```

## repo.default

The repo category `--repo` assumes when given bare (no `<cat>` argument): the name of a
[repo.category.\<cat\>](#repocategorycat) entry, one of the built-ins (`remote`, `local`) or
your own.

```toml
[repo.default]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Default repo category when --repo is bare: a [repo.category.<cat>] name: a built-in (remote, local) or your own"
used-by = "--repo (default category when --repo is bare)"
example = "acmehousing"
```

## repo.category.\<cat\>

The literal value behind a repo category name: a remote url prefix (`init` appends
`/<NAME>.git`) or a local parent directory. `init` resolves `--repo <cat>` through this table
when its target is a path or a bare name.

```toml
[repo.category."<cat>"]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Literal value for repo category <cat>: a remote URL prefix (init appends /<NAME>.git) or a local parent dir"
used-by = "--repo <cat> (init remote/local resolution)"
example = "git@github.com:acmehousing"
```

## account.\<name\>.repo.default

Per-account variant of [repo.default](#repodefault): the default category used while the
`<name>` account profile is active.

```toml
[account."<name>".repo.default]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Per-account default repo category: a [repo.category.<cat>] name: a built-in (remote, local) or your own"
used-by = "--account <name> with --repo"
example = "acmehousing"
```

## account.\<name\>.repo.category.\<cat\>

Per-account variant of [repo.category.\<cat\>](#repocategorycat): a category defined inside an
account profile, shadowing the top-level table while that account is active.

```toml
[account."<name>".repo.category."<cat>"]
homes = ["user"]
kind = "str"
doc = "Per-account literal value for repo category <cat> (remote URL prefix or local parent dir)"
used-by = "--account <name> with --repo <cat>"
example = "git@github.com:acmehousing"
```

## bot-session.items

The default item set the `bot-session` conversation view renders, a comma-separated list (e.g.
`headers,user,assistant,tool,summary`). The per-item `--<item>` / `--no-<item>` flags override
individual items, and `--all` / `--none` replace the base set entirely.

```toml
[bot-session.items]
homes = ["user", "workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]
kind = "item-list"
doc = "Default bot-session item set (comma-separated)"
used-by = "bot-session --<item> / --no-<item> / --all / --none"
default = "headers,user,assistant,tool,summary"
```

## bot-session.result-lines

Maximum lines shown per tool result in the conversation view when results are rendered; `0`
means unlimited. The `--result-lines` flag overrides it.

```toml
[bot-session.result-lines]
homes = ["user", "workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]
kind = "usize"
doc = "Default --result-lines: max lines shown per tool result (0 = unlimited)"
used-by = "bot-session --result-lines"
default = 10
```

## bot-session.col-width

First-column width in `bot-session`'s field-inventory views: `--fields`, `--unknown`, and
`--per-line`. The conversation view never consults it. The built-in default aligns the type
column for ~99% of observed key paths: every structural key except a long tail of
`snapshot.trackedFileBackups.<absolute path>.*` keys, whose embedded absolute paths can be
arbitrarily long and so are left to overflow. The `--col-width` flag overrides it.

```toml
[bot-session.col-width]
homes = ["user", "workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]
kind = "usize"
doc = "Default --col-width: first-column width in the --fields / --unknown / --per-line views"
used-by = "bot-session --col-width"
default = 68
```

## repos.work

The work repo's path, relative to the config file's directory: `"."` in the work repo, `".."`
in the bot repo. Structural: written by `init`, read by workspace-root discovery, and the entry
that resolves to the config's own directory names that file's side. Every instance config must
carry it.

```toml
[repos.work]
homes = ["workspace-code", "workspace-bot"]
kind = "str"
doc = "The work repo's path, relative to this config file's directory (\".\" in the work repo, \"..\" in the bot repo); the entry resolving to the config's own directory names the side"
used-by = "find_workspace_root, side detection (structural; written by init)"
required = true
example = "."
```

## repos.bot

The bot repo's path, relative to the config file's directory (e.g. `".claude"` in the work
repo, `"."` in the bot repo). Its presence is what signals dual-repo mode; a single-repo
workspace simply omits it.

```toml
[repos.bot]
